summary: In Auric's radiant but strained Crown Ring, a returning resident discovers her parents' temporarily empty apartment was assigned to new refugees. Halev, elected Auric leader and head of the wider Verge council, faces two legitimate housing claims.
settingText: INT. AURIC BAZAAR — LUXURY RING CONCOURSE — MORNING

dialogueInline.speaker: Resident
dialogueInline.text: My parents still live in that apartment. Their belongings are inside.

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: The placement office told us it was vacant. We didn't know.

dialogueInline.speaker: Resident
dialogueInline.text: They left yesterday to stay with my brother. They were coming back.

dialogueInline.speaker: Paul
dialogueInline.text: We can take our things and move.

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: You collapsed on the walk here. You're not sleeping in the corridor.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: Nobody is being evicted today. This family can stay until we find another room.

dialogueInline.speaker: Sera
dialogueInline.text: And when her parents return? They have nowhere else.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: Then I need to find room for them too. I can't promise how quickly.

panelPlan: Elegant chandelier concourse converted into a crowded shelter, preserving costly finishes against uncomfortable crowding and limited warming space.
A resident confronts Richard at her sealed family apartment.
Paul moves protectively between the adults.
Halev arrives as Dain refuses an easy eviction.
Both families remain on opposite sides of one doorway.
directionInline: Make the luxury ring feel like contested shelter rather than reclaimed housing: refugee bedding, old family possessions and civic staff should occupy the same doorway. No one is clearly wrong, and Halev's inability to promise where the resident family goes must remain visible.

directionInline.text: Establish clearly that the apartment belonged to a resident family temporarily away, not an abandoned home. Halev grants temporary shelter rather than resolving the housing shortage. Keep the resident and refugee families equally recognizable as individuals.

directionInline: Auric is genuinely beautiful, functioning and prosperous. Rooms may be temporarily vacant but privately owned, inadequately heated, structurally unsafe or politically unavailable. Halev cannot manufacture warm space by decree.

summary: The returning Auric resident's elderly mother has breathing trouble when the contested apartment's heat fails. Richard uses scarce medicine but all households need a sustainable heating solution.
settingText: INT. LUXURY RING — TEMPORARY APARTMENT

dialogueInline.speaker: Resident
dialogueInline.text: My mother's breathing changed when the heat went out. Please do something.

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: How long has she been struggling? Has she taken any medication?

dialogueInline.speaker: Resident
dialogueInline.text: Nothing. She was managing until the room got cold.

dialogueInline.speaker: Paul
dialogueInline.text: Dad, her breathing's getting worse.

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: Hold the light steady. I have medicine left from Tal Corvus.

dialogueInline.speaker: Resident
dialogueInline.text: That's all you have for your own people.

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: She's the patient in front of me. Help me sit her upright.

dialogueInline.speaker: Sera
dialogueInline.text: Is the medicine enough?

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: It will help, but she needs steady heat. We may have to move her again.

dialogueInline.speaker: Resident
dialogueInline.text: Tell me what to do.

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: Wrap the blankets around her shoulders. Keep talking to her.

panelPlan: Emergency lights and visible breath crowd both families together.
The returning resident's elderly mother is struggling to breathe while seated; no harmed child.
Richard opens his last field kit.
Paul steadies the lamp while the resident supports her elderly mother in a sitting position.
The older woman breathes easier after treatment, but no one knows how long the room will remain warm.
directionInline: This is the FIRST treatment of the returning resident's elderly mother, an adult. The medical treatment improves her breathing temporarily; she struggles again under the same failing heat on P07.
The emergency interrupts rather than resolves a legitimate property dispute; Richard uses scarce medicine on the adult resident patient while both households need warmth.
Use physically plausible and humane adult medical care. Do not show harmed or endangered children.

summary: Venn leaves Auric for Fleet tribunal as a committed Core officer who accepts accountability. Naomi, responsible for the cold and crowded arrivals, challenges her understanding of the rescue's unfinished consequences.
settingText: INT. AURIC DOCK — DEPARTURE GLASS

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Fleet has relieved you of Thunderbreak, and you're still going to their tribunal?

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: I gave the order. My crew shouldn't answer for that choice.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Keating already told the Admiralty her version.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: Then they'll hear mine. I gave the order to turn back.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: And you'll be gone when Auric has to feed and heat everyone you saved.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: I know the rescue didn't finish when we docked.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: You don't know what it's costing the people living here.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: Not enough. I should have asked before I left.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Come back with more than an explanation.

panelPlan: Venn's escort shuttle waits beyond immense glass.
Naomi blocks Venn's path.
Their controlled anger closes the distance.
Venn almost reaches for Naomi and stops.
Venn boards while Naomi remains reflected beside the shuttle.
directionInline: Naomi's anger is about asymmetry of consequence, not abandonment. Keep the departing shuttle and Auric's damaged public space in the same visual field so Venn literally leaves the place Naomi must continue managing.

directionInline.text: The tribunal summons and provisional loss of Thunderbreak's command must be understandable before Venn departs. Naomi's anger is about Auric bearing the ongoing cost, not opposition to rescuing civilians.

directionInline: Venn is fundamentally of the Core: she believes in Fleet's BHA inheritance, service traditions and institutional mission. Her frontline experiences challenge decisions, not that identity.

summary: At the tribunal Venn accepts the two refusals: diverting Thunderbreak from Auric's heat-and-medicine convoy to save a civilian ship, and declining to separate mixed patients. Dominion takes seriously the risk to thousands whose supplies weren't protected; Venn speaks to the people dying in front of her.
settingText: INT. DAWNWARD HORIZON — ADMIRALTY TRIBUNAL — DAY

dialogueInline.speaker: Dominion
dialogueInline.text: Commodore, were you ordered to remain with the authorized supply convoy?

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: I received that order. I took Thunderbreak to Mercy of Dawn.

dialogueInline.speaker: Keating
dialogueInline.text: That exposed Auric's heat and medicine. Some of the cargo never arrived.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kerr
dialogueInline.text: The passenger hull was losing pressure under attack. Her turn kept those people alive.

dialogueInline.speaker: Keating
dialogueInline.text: You later refused an order governing Shard patients still in Fleet custody.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: Those patients were part of mixed care groups. The order would have separated them.

dialogueInline.speaker: Dominion
dialogueInline.text: The convoy carried medicine and heat for thousands. You were assigned to protect them too.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: Enter both refusals. Enter the people saved alongside the supplies we failed to deliver.

panelPlan: Venn stands alone below the circular Admiralty dais while Dominion establishes the direct order to guard the supply convoy.
Keating displays the diverted freighter, Billie's attack at the Shatterwake exit, the recovered but damaged supply spine and the gap in Auric's delivered relief.
Venn acknowledges the first refusal without claiming the cargo loss was immaterial; Dominion introduces the second order to detain Shard arrivals in Fleet custody.
Kerr activates civilian testimony from those rescued, including the mixed patients whose caregivers would have been separated. The evidence is practical, human and contested.
Venn accepts both command charges; behind her the displayed rescue and cargo loss remain visible as parallel consequences.
directionInline: The tribunal must confront two recorded refusals: leaving the authorized supply screen to save refugees, and declining Fleet detention of mixed Shard patients. Present the partially recovered supply spine, missing cargo and civilian testimony together. Keep the hearing grounded in the actual Shatterwake engagement.
Dominion is a sincere institutionalist, not an antagonist seeking civilian suffering. His ambition to make Fleet routes permanent and his service ethic reinforce one another.

Neither Fleet officer counts the Shard households fed by stolen provisions as equivalent beneficiaries of the convoy's loss; they are aware of piracy but measure losses from the original recipients' perspective.

summary: Richard proves that specific Triarch authorities deliberately cut heating and medicine to protesting Shard districts in Tal Corvus. Political deprivation within Shard society is different from ordinary frontier cargo raiding.
settingText: INT. AURIC LUXURY RING — IMPROVISED CLINIC

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: These patients came from different districts. Why do their injuries look the same?

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: Their heat and medical power failed in the same way.

dialogueInline.speaker: Paul
dialogueInline.text: But the official reports say each district had a separate equipment failure.

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: Look at the timestamps. Each district lost supply after it protested Triarch orders.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: You're saying someone chose which district went cold.

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: The distribution orders show it. Their supplies were diverted while other districts stayed online.

dialogueInline.speaker: Paul
dialogueInline.text: The public reports don't match the clinic copies.

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: They changed those reports twice. I kept the originals.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: If this leaves Auric, the Triarch will know you have them.

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: They've been trying to get these records back since Tal Corvus.

panelPlan: Richard treats patients from several Tal Corvus districts while the Auric clinic also serves locals.
Tess compares similar clinical effects in patient charts; Richard opens the corresponding original distribution records.
Paul places separately dated official failure claims beside synchronized diversion orders; the contradiction is visible and specific.
Richard identifies the connection between public protests, selected district shutdowns and preserved records; Tess sees the motive.
Richard closes his field archive as nearby patients continue needing care; the records are evidence with a real chain of custody, not mystical revelations.
directionInline: Treat the discovery as forensic work: mismatched official reports, clinic copies, utility timestamps and district maps. The evidence proves selective punitive shutdowns inside broader scarcity; do not imply every shortage in the frontier was fabricated.

directionInline.text: Evidence must prove intentional district selection, not merely correlation. Distinguish power failures from diverted medical supply and show original clinic copies versus subsequently revised official reports. All on-screen text beyond scripted wording must remain unreadable.

directionInline: Ground records in measured utility and medical evidence, not mystical objects. Individual Shard civilians suffered; avoid imputing each Triarch act to all captains or all Shards.

summary: Halev and Dain confront insufficient warmed housing in a beautiful Verge hub. The fast Green Corridor amplifies Auric's existing pressure by accelerating relocation and commerce; real ownership and capacity limits remain.
settingText: INT. AURIC BAZAAR — CIVIC CHAMBER

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: We can't send the Tal Corvus families back. I want the next residential section opened.

dialogueInline.speaker: Sera
dialogueInline.text: That section lost its heat overnight. We can't move people into rooms that are freezing.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: Then where do we put the families still sleeping in the concourse?

dialogueInline.speaker: Wallace
dialogueInline.text: Some owners might agree to short-term leases if we cover their costs.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: People are already sleeping six to a room. Finding the rent still won't make those rooms warm.

dialogueInline.speaker: Sera
dialogueInline.text: My district is taking the overflow. Our heaters and supplies are running out.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: How many rooms can we safely use today?

dialogueInline.speaker: Sera
dialogueInline.text: I'll give you the count, including the homes that volunteered space. Then we tell everyone the actual limits.

panelPlan: The crowded chamber overlooks refugees beyond glass.
Halev asks for an extension.
Dain shows failing residential levels.
Wallace's market answer is rejected.
Naomi makes Halev name the harmed district.
directionInline: Sera should control the room by forcing costs into names and places. Keep the failing district map visible while Wallace offers a market abstraction and Naomi reacts too aggressively, allowing Sera—not Naomi—to define the civilian political question.

directionInline.text: The scene must make a practical decision: assess heated capacity before promising more rooms. Remove rhetorical threats and market caricature. Wallace may advocate pricing but is not shown as an inhuman straw man.

directionInline: Halev is Auric's elected leader and council head for the wider Verge, not a dictator over independently owned homes.
The corridor expands opportunity and the speed of migration without causing every existing shortage. Resident and merchant concerns are legitimate.

summary: The returning resident's elderly mother struggles again in the shared warming room. The Luminara mother contributes her family's good blanket while Richard and nineteen-year-old Paul coordinate her care.
settingText: INT. LUXURY RING — WARMING ROOM

dialogueInline.speaker: Boy
dialogueInline.text: Why is it colder in this room than outside?

dialogueInline.speaker: Paul
dialogueInline.text: One heater for too many people. It isn't keeping up.

dialogueInline.speaker: Resident
dialogueInline.text: Mum's wheezing again. The medicine helped, but only for a while.

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: Sit her up. Keep her chest clear of the blankets.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mother
dialogueInline.text: Use ours. It's warmer than that one.

dialogueInline.speaker: Resident
dialogueInline.text: Your family needs it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mother
dialogueInline.text: She needs it right now.

dialogueInline.speaker: Paul
dialogueInline.text: Can you hold the light while I help Dad?

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: Keep talking to her while I check her breathing.

dialogueInline.speaker: Resident
dialogueInline.text: Doctor, there's room beside her now.

panelPlan: Families pack around one improvised heater.
The resident's elderly mother struggles to breathe while seated, attended by adults.
Refugees surrender blanket and space.
Paul holds the lamp and helps organize blankets while Richard treats the adult patient.
The resident mother makes room for Richard.
directionInline: This is not full reconciliation. The families share a blanket and the warmth of an inadequate room because the same adult elder is struggling to breathe, with guarded body language and practical medical care.
Continue the elderly patient from P02. Cold and failing heat drive the recurrence, not a new unrelated medical emergency. No endangered children.
The Luminara family remains recently relocated civilian migrants in a prosperous hub with more demand for warmth than capacity.

summary: Jex's cultivated network of information and favors begins backfiring as Tali warns that the routes protecting hidden families are exposed. He once believed independent captains would preserve the commerce they depend on.
settingText: INT. VEIL MARKET — JEX'S OFFICE / TALI'S SAFEHOUSE

dialogueInline.speaker: Tali
dialogueInline.text: Three people asked for your Auric passage by name. None of them had families aboard.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jex
dialogueInline.text: Or somebody leaked a crossing window. We've both seen how that works.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tali
dialogueInline.text: Or following the people using it. Either way it's not safe anymore.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jex
dialogueInline.text: I'll close the public access after the ships already in transit clear.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tali
dialogueInline.text: Close it now. The people hunting you are getting closer to my safehouse.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jex
dialogueInline.text: I've got families waiting, and two pilots who owe me a crossing.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tali
dialogueInline.text: And I'm sheltering families here. They're the ones who'll pay if my doors get exposed.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jex
dialogueInline.text: Your private network stays off the board. I won't touch it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tali
dialogueInline.text: Make certain you keep that promise.

panelPlan: Jex is surrounded by competing demands.
A private distorted-glass call resolves into Tali.
Her refuge quietly prepares to disappear.
Jex receives another plea from trapped families.
His hands hover between closing and accepting the route.
directionInline: Tali's refuge should look operational and vulnerable: packed bags, erased route marks and people preparing to move. Jex's hesitation must occur between two real groups of people who both need the same network.

directionInline.text: Establish that the publicly known passage and Tali's private haven network are different physical route systems. Jex promises not to expose her network now, making P20-P21 a costly reversal, not a route invented mid-crisis.

directionInline: Jex knowingly leaks ship movements and crossing timings to multiple factions for reciprocal favors, and mistakes the incentives of trade for a power to control others. Tali isn't a pawn and insists on protecting her own families.

summary: The Trade Mask's offer to renew commerce in exchange for Richard's surrender puts Shard material needs against the risk of political coercion. Tal Corvus's records make the promise uncertain.
settingText: INT. IMPROVISED CLINIC — BROADCAST LIGHT

dialogueInline.speaker: Trade Mask
dialogueInline.text: Deliver Richard Secundo. Reject Fleet occupation of Auric. We will restore trade and offer amnesty.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: They cut supplies to districts that protested them. They can cut Auric off again.

dialogueInline.speaker: Paul
dialogueInline.text: Dad, if you went back, would they stop threatening this station?

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: They'd have me and the records. That's what they're offering to trade for.

dialogueInline.speaker: Paul
dialogueInline.text: But could your surrender keep everyone here safe?

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: I don't know. There's no reason to trust their promise.

dialogueInline.speaker: Paul
dialogueInline.text: Are you still thinking about it?

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: I'm thinking about the people they'll hurt if I refuse. And the people they'll hurt if I believe them.

panelPlan: Clinic screens seize into a masked broadcast.
The Triarch promises restored trade and amnesty.
Richard is publicly labeled thief and traitor.
Paul studies his father while patients watch.
Richard kills the screen but cannot answer him.
directionInline: Introduce the Silent Triarch as a three-mask council while the Trade Mask alone speaks the offer. Raid and Fear remain silent in the background. The visual distinction between the masks should be readable without explanatory captions so later differences feel like an existing structure, not a retcon.

directionInline.text: Preserve the Triarch's three distinct political masks, but make the offer explicitly conditional. Richard knows surrender risks both himself and the preserved evidence; do not let Paul's question evaporate in vague familial sentiment.

directionInline: Triarch masks embody distinct political interests, not magic; independent Shard captains are not automatically bound by every masked authority. Paul remains a nineteen-year-old autonomous adult.

summary: Abby risks her Shard standing by warning Auric and seeking independent captains willing to protect civilian transports against Billie and Pike. She cannot command the confederation.
settingText: INT./EXT. AURIC SECURITY LOCK

dialogueInline.speaker: Sera
dialogueInline.text: Keep your ships outside Auric's defense line. You can enter alone and unarmed.

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: They're staying back. My weapons are in the lock.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: Why take the risk of coming here?

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: Billie and Pike are gathering captains. They're preparing to attack Auric because Richard's records are spreading.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: What do you want from us?

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: To warn you while there's still time to move civilians. I know captains who may shield the evacuation, if you'll let them come.

dialogueInline.speaker: Sera
dialogueInline.text: We can't hand Auric's defenses to another Shard commander.

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: Then don't. If any agree, coordinate them through Naomi. Just don't wait for the attack.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: Open the lock. Naomi stays with her.

panelPlan: Abby's tiny shuttle waits while Scythe remains distant.
She places her weapons in the lock tray.
Dain faces her through armored glass.
Abby shows Pike and Billie's gathering force.
Halev opens the door while Naomi remains ready.
directionInline: Abby earns entry by arriving physically alone and disarmed while her warship remains outside. Sera owns the political skepticism, Naomi owns the security risk, and Halev accepts personal responsibility for opening the door.

directionInline.text: Her offer on this page sets up Naomi's conditional acceptance of six Shard defectors on P23. Abby's political and military authority is distinct from Billie's and Pike's.

directionInline: Abby's proposed change risks both practical command alliances and Shard personal and cultural identity. She must persuade fellow captains, not order them.

summary: Abby urges her sister Tessa to leave the clinic; Tess accepts her own history as a Shard commander, though she did not order the Triarch's district cutoffs. Their affection remains real even under disagreement.
settingText: INT. AURIC LUXURY RING — CLINIC PASSAGE

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: Billie and Pike are taking ships toward Auric. I can't protect you if you stay in this clinic.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: I know where they're headed. I've been helping the people their crews drove out.

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: Come with me. I can't lose you here too.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: I commanded a ship through those years. I knew people were going cold.

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: We didn't make the shutdown orders.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: We kept sailing. I told myself keeping my crew alive was enough.

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: Staying here won't undo what happened.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: I'm not trying to undo it. These patients need me now.

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: Then keep the token. If you change your mind, I can find you.

panelPlan: The sisters see each other across the crowded clinic.
Abby offers Tess her command token.
Tess continues dressing a civilian wound.
Abby absorbs the refusal.
The token remains on an empty cot between them.
directionInline: The sisters' history should sit in the unused command token between them. Tess keeps treating patients throughout the argument, making staying an action she is already performing rather than a declaration about who she has become.

directionInline.text: Make the distinction between Triarch policy responsibility, Shard leaders' prior failures to challenge harm, and the immediate Billie/Pike attack explicit. Tess does not claim she or Abby ordered the Triarch shutdowns.

directionInline: Tessa and Abby are sisters and Billie is their close sister-in-arms. Neither woman is a retrospective moral innocent; Tessa feels complicit because she stayed in command while civilians were harmed.

summary: Kerr offers Venn a defensible interpretation of her rescue through Fleet interests. She refuses to claim strategic motives she didn't have and accepts professional accountability without rejecting the institution she serves.
settingText: INT. ADMIRALTY TRIBUNAL — RECESS ALCOVE

dialogueInline.speaker: Kerr
dialogueInline.text: You can argue that returning for the evacuation ship protected Fleet interests.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: That wasn't my reason. Those people were going to die.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kerr
dialogueInline.text: Saving them also protected Auric. It's a defense the tribunal may accept.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: It wasn't my calculation when I turned the ship. I won't tell the tribunal it was.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kerr
dialogueInline.text: If you challenge the order itself, Dominion will remove you from command.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: He's already taken Thunderbreak. I won't pretend I obeyed an order I deliberately rejected.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kerr
dialogueInline.text: The written finding will follow you long after this hearing.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: Then I want it to say what I actually did.

panelPlan: Venn and Kerr stand behind a translucent screen.
Kerr offers the prepared defense.
Venn deletes it.
Kerr warns her what honesty costs.
Venn returns without notes.
directionInline: Kerr's proposed defense should look genuinely useful, not cowardly. Venn deletes the argument because it is false, forcing the tribunal to judge the actual choice instead of allowing the scene to become a purity test.

directionInline.text: Kerr's advice must be a plausible legal defense, not simply an invitation to lie. Venn explicitly chooses a more dangerous truthful account. Do not imply the ship's command has not already been suspended.

directionInline: Kerr's counsel is plausible rather than corrupt. Venn remains invested in Fleet discipline, despite taking frontline consequences seriously.

summary: Admiralty withdraws Thunderbreak and finite temporary medical-power support while Venn's authority is suspended. Fleet's force-allocation and legal logic leaves Auric colder, without requiring Dominion to want anyone to suffer.
settingText: INT. AURIC ESCORT CONTROL / LUXURY RING

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: AURIC — AFTER FLEET'S WITHDRAWAL ORDER.

dialogueInline.speaker: Deka
dialogueInline.text: Thunderbreak has been ordered beyond Auric's defense boundary.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Who's giving that order while Venn's at the tribunal?

dialogueInline.speaker: Deka
dialogueInline.text: Admiralty command. Commodore Venn's authority is suspended.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: Fleet's temporary medical and power teams are being reassigned with the ship.

dialogueInline.speaker: Sera
dialogueInline.text: Those heaters struggled before the Fleet teams came. They're worse without them.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: They can call it redeployment. We still need heat by tonight.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: Can Venn stop this from the tribunal?

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Not from where she's standing. We have to keep the clinics running ourselves.

panelPlan: Naomi receives the withdrawal order.
Thunderbreak recedes beyond Auric jurisdiction.
The clinic loses a Fleet power feed.
Dain sees a shelter level go dark.
Naomi closes Venn's personal channel without calling.
directionInline: Show the withdrawal as material loss: a power feed goes dark, medical support disappears and Thunderbreak moves beyond the boundary. Sera and Naomi should experience the same act through different lenses—punishment and leverage.

directionInline.text: State clearly who issued withdrawal, Venn's actual authority, and the immediate civilian consequence. The brief caption marks a temporal move without introducing a narrator.

directionInline: The heating problems predate Fleet aid and increase with rapid migration; emergency Fleet power assistance was real, limited and temporary.
Do not depict Dominion deliberately withholding heat to terrify residents. He can regard redeployment as strategically or institutionally justified while failing to feel the local cost.

summary: Richard agrees to public testimony with original evidence while refusing forced custody or a Fleet occupation rationale. His adult son Paul decides for himself whether to appear.
settingText: INT. AURIC ARCHIVE BOOTH — NIGHT

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: If you broadcast from Auric, the Triarch will know exactly where you are.

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: They already know. They demanded I surrender on a public transmission.

dialogueInline.speaker: Sera
dialogueInline.text: Before we begin, what conditions do you want on the record?

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: I won't go into Fleet custody. And I won't testify in support of Fleet troops occupying Auric.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: The records still need to be available for anyone to check.

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: All the original clinic copies. The dates and distribution orders too.

dialogueInline.speaker: Sera
dialogueInline.text: And Paul?

dialogueInline.speaker: Paul
dialogueInline.text: I'm nineteen. I'll decide whether to speak. I don't want my face on the feed.

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: You won't be on camera.

dialogueInline.speaker: Paul
dialogueInline.text: Then go ahead. People need to know what happened.

panelPlan: An independent evidence-and-broadcast booth waits dark: practical public-record infrastructure with a camera, source-file access, provenance checks, and tamper indicators rather than a ceremonial archive space.
Halev warns that a transmission from Auric makes the station a target.
Richard sets conditions limiting how his evidence may be used.
Paul refuses the seat beside him and Richard accepts the decision.
Dain activates the tamper-evident public feed and places Richard’s conditions at its beginning.
directionInline: The archive booth is ordinary evidence infrastructure. Richard's conditions must appear in the public record before his testimony begins, and Paul's refusal of the camera should be accepted without turning him into a symbolic witness.

directionInline.text: Richard's conditions are his stated limits, not an implausible guarantee governing all later political uses of public evidence. Make the source-file attachments concrete. Paul is 19 and decides for himself; keep him off-camera.

directionInline: Paul Secundo is nineteen. Evidence is practical measured records with clear provenance, not sacred archival material.

summary: Richard's evidence names individual Tal Corvus adults deprived of heat or medicine by specific political decisions; listeners independently preserve copies and contest the official record.
settingText: INT. AURIC ARCHIVE / INTERCUT TAL CORVUS

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: Nemi Vale. Forty-two. Her breathing equipment lost power when her district's supply was cut.

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: Ors Dane. His district protested. The next delivery contained no antibiotics.

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: Sergeant Pell. He carried medicine into a sealed district. They arrested and executed him for theft.

dialogueInline.speaker: Paul
dialogueInline.text: I remember these people. He treated all three.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: Then don't let their names disappear behind a casualty count.

dialogueInline.speaker: Listener
dialogueInline.text: My sister lived in Dane's district. Send me those records.

dialogueInline.speaker: Another Listener
dialogueInline.text: Copy the feed before they cut it off.

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: The official reports call these shortages. The original orders show who was cut off, and when.

panelPlan: Richard sits alone before the camera with source records visibly paired to the testimony feed so named people remain tied to specific clinical and policy evidence.
Nemi Vale's adult clinical record is paired with the preserved power-supply evidence and the remembered face of the adult patient Richard treated.
A Shard engine crew stops work to listen.
Paul hears familiar people and districts named outside the booth.
Anonymous hands retransmit the testimony and supporting data before authorities can suppress the channel.
directionInline: Nemi Vale is forty-two. Her breathing-equipment failure is shown through authentic medical and utility evidence. If a patient image is used it depicts an adult.
No harmed or deceased minors are depicted or named in this testimony. Focus on the adult victims, original records, source provenance and the ordinary listeners redistributing them.
Evidence and individual histories remain measurable and human, never a mystical revelation or invented interface script.

summary: Pike proposes sabotage of Auric's heat; Billie agrees to it as part of capturing Richard. Under fear of losing captains and Shard identity, she crosses from cargo piracy into deliberate endangerment of civilians.
settingText: INT. BROKEN OATH — WAR ROOM

dialogueInline.speaker: Pike
dialogueInline.text: Richard's broadcast has the captains questioning the Triarch. Abby's people are using it against us.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: He's showing what happened to those districts. Some of our crews were there.

dialogueInline.speaker: Pike
dialogueInline.text: Then stop him. My people can cut Auric's heat exchanger before we arrive.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: You'll turn residents against refugees. Somebody could die in that panic.

dialogueInline.speaker: Pike
dialogueInline.text: A riot keeps Auric's guards occupied while we get into the clinic.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: Do it away from the clinic. Secundo comes out alive. He'll answer for this in front of everyone.

dialogueInline.speaker: Pike
dialogueInline.text: And if he refuses?

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: Then everyone sees what it costs to defy us.

panelPlan: Richard's testimony remains visible aboard Broken Oath; Billie reacts to the named civilians and original record images.
Pike shows Auric's ring and service systems, identifying a heat-exchange target already reachable by planted Shard saboteurs.
Billie objects when Pike acknowledges the likely civilian disorder; he shows how it opens a path toward Richard's clinic.
Billie orders Richard captured alive so he can be publicly confronted, revealing she is willing to endanger civilians to protect her leadership.
Pike sends the sabotage order while Billie takes control of the assault plan.
directionInline: Billie should react to one named victim before Pike turns the testimony into an attack opportunity. Her agreement to strike Auric is therefore a choice to answer uncomfortable truth with spectacle, not ignorance of what Richard said.

directionInline.text: This is the CAUSAL START of P17 sabotage and the P22 assault. It must be obvious who plans the exchanger cut and who authorizes it. The plan is military-political coercion, not abstract villain rhetoric. Avoid suggesting Billie personally planted the insignia.

directionInline: Billie owns the decision. Her cultural grievance and historical anger are real but not absolution, and she must never look like a generic sadistic raider.

summary: Pike's operatives cut an exchanger and plant a misleading medical patch. Auric residents feel the threat of cold and crowding while Halev insists that physical sabotage does not by itself identify the perpetrator.
settingText: INT. LUXURY RING — HEAT EXCHANGE / CONCOURSE

dialogueInline.speaker: Resident
dialogueInline.text: That medical patch was beside the broken exchanger. It looks like the doctor's.

dialogueInline.speaker: Refugee
dialogueInline.text: He's been treating your families. Why would he shut off our heat?

dialogueInline.speaker: Another Resident
dialogueInline.text: Those Shard ships brought trouble here. How do we know who came with them?

dialogueInline.speaker: Paul
dialogueInline.text: Stop pushing her. She's carrying a child.

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: Paul, stay with me. Don't let them separate us.

dialogueInline.speaker: Sera
dialogueInline.text: Move away from the damaged equipment. Everyone needs the same emergency heat.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: The exchanger was cut by hand. This was sabotage.

dialogueInline.speaker: Resident
dialogueInline.text: Then who did it?

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: We don't know. Someone left a patch here, and I'm not calling that proof.

panelPlan: A covert Shard sleeper, face withheld but visibly matching Pike's operational gear from P16, physically cuts an accessible exchanger connection and places a stolen-style medical patch.
The adjacent heating circuit loses function; emergency illumination comes on while the vulnerable residential ring cools.
A resident picks up the planted patch at the damaged service hatch, shows it to others, and an argument starts.
The crowd presses toward Richard and Paul; Richard shields vulnerable patients while Sera clears the area.
Halev and a technician inspect tool marks on the exchanger, confirming sabotage but not who performed it.
directionInline: The planted insignia must look almost too convenient once Halev sees the physical damage. Let the crowd's fear become dangerous before officials can explain anything; Richard protecting Paul should precede any argument about evidence.

directionInline.text: This sabotage is a deliberate action ordered by Pike and permitted by Billie, not an unexplained mechanical failure. The medical patch is planted and NOT proof of Richard's guilt. Avoid portraying the sleeper as a generic pirate or making the planted patch a magical plot token.

directionInline: Preserve polished Auric ring details and coherent industrial piping/exchanger damage. Failing heat doesn't instantly ice over a pressurized station.

summary: Halev, Dain and Naomi issue honest emergency instructions showing exactly which rooms retain heat and where residents must move, rather than obscuring the danger after sabotage.
settingText: INT. AURIC CIVIC BROADCAST PLATFORM

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: If we tell everyone the heating system could fail, they'll rush the shelter exits.

dialogueInline.speaker: Sera
dialogueInline.text: The exchanger is destroyed. Our crews can't keep all these rooms warm.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: People are already moving. They need to know which areas still have heat.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: We can't promise the next shelter will be any safer.

dialogueInline.speaker: Sera
dialogueInline.text: Then we say that too. We can still guide people away from the damaged section.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: We need time to move the patients.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Give them directions now. Richard's clinic can't wait for us to agree on a perfect plan.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: The luxury ring's heating is failing. Move toward the inner shelter with the people who need help walking.

panelPlan: The three argue while a crowd pounds the doors.
Halev asks for delay.
Dain demands evacuation.
Naomi activates the live feed mid-argument.
They face the frightened station together.
directionInline: Naomi should activate the broadcast while the leaders are still disagreeing, denying them the chance to polish a unified message. The public hears uncertainty and argument along with the evacuation warning.

directionInline.text: No generic political speech about honesty. Tie dialogue to specific heating damage, vulnerable patients and the route to inner shelter. Keep the existing public broadcast as practical emergency instructions, not a new framing device.

directionInline: Evacuation depends on measured temperatures, known passages and escort teams. No convenient magic warming or instantaneous citywide catastrophe.

summary: An emergency order intended to prioritize existing residents inadvertently bars newly arrived refugees from warm shelter. Halev publicly corrects his own elected government's mistake and residents share limited space.
settingText: INT. AURIC INNER SHELTER GATE

dialogueInline.speaker: Guard
dialogueInline.text: The shelter order puts registered Auric residents first. I can't admit people without local registration.

dialogueInline.speaker: Paul
dialogueInline.text: We're the ones they moved into this ring. Where are we supposed to go now?

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: Keep your bag. I'll find a place where we can wait.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: Stop turning people away. Who authorized this restriction?

dialogueInline.speaker: Guard
dialogueInline.text: It's in your emergency priority order. I was told to enforce it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: Then I signed an order that doesn't cover the people we invited here. Let them through.

dialogueInline.speaker: Sera
dialogueInline.text: My family's berth is number twelve. Give it to the next family in line.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: Sera, where will your family sleep?

dialogueInline.speaker: Sera
dialogueInline.text: With the other households sharing rooms. They shouldn't lose shelter because they arrived yesterday.

dialogueInline.speaker: Resident
dialogueInline.text: Are they letting the Tal Corvus families in now?

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: Yes. Help them bring the children and the injured inside.

panelPlan: Officials privilege registered residents.
Richard turns away with Paul.
Halev tears up his own authorization.
Dain gives away her family berth.
Mixed families enter while both leaders remain outside.
directionInline: Halev and Sera give up privileged access before asking anyone else to share. Their families and security remain unresolved outside the frame; the point is not martyrdom but removing an exemption they cannot ethically defend.

directionInline.text: Establish the order as a real administrative mistake with immediate consequences; Halev reverses it explicitly. Avoid implying a single surrendered berth can house all displaced residents. Show several residents choosing to assist, not a magically unanimous crowd.

directionInline: Halev bears responsibility for his order, but his voters' concern about heat and private space remains valid. Correction costs actual capacity.

summary: Jex and Naomi weigh exposing Tali's concealed network to protect evacuation craft. His business in routes, timing, ship movements and traded favors has created real obligations he cannot control.
settingText: INT. JEX'S OFFICE / TALI SAFEHOUSE / AURIC MAP

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: The public passage is under enemy observation. Evacuation ships will fly straight into their weapons.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jex
dialogueInline.text: Tali warned me somebody was tracking it. I closed the public entry too late.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Do you have another route into Auric?

dialogueInline.speaker: Jex
dialogueInline.text: There's a private network. Its approaches pass shelters I helped keep off public charts.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tali
dialogueInline.text: Including this safehouse. You promised it would stay off the maps.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jex
dialogueInline.text: Using it now will expose the access points to anyone watching the traffic.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: We can escort ships once they reach Auric. I can't protect every place they depart from.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tali
dialogueInline.text: People at the public passage will die if we do nothing. Give me time to warn the safehouses.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jex
dialogueInline.text: I'll wait for your signal. Then we open the routes.

panelPlan: Naomi's live traffic picture identifies a public corridor lined with hostile contacts and incoming civilian transports.
Jex brings up a separate private network of authenticated routes; it includes multiple inhabited safehouses rather than empty coordinates.
Tali appears from one working haven and objects because use will reveal the system's access points.
Jex and Naomi identify the ships they can shield near Auric and the departure points they cannot defend.
Tali begins a hurried warning to the families at her safehouse; Jex holds the transmission until she signals readiness.
directionInline: The hidden route network should be clearly larger than Jex's already-public passage. Tali's haven is one node among many, so opening the system saves Auric by exposing the people who made Jex's private advantage possible.

directionInline.text: Tali knowingly accepts the risk and issues a warning before Jex exposes her network. This pays off P08's promise and gives P21 a concrete cost. Corridors are physical beacon/field routes, not teleportation portals or fantasy magical circles.

directionInline: This scene does not become an expository thesis about zero-sum raids. The families hidden at Jex's routes belong to multiple factions.

Jex has a partial insight: resources captured from Verge shipments can feed Shard communities, while the violence and damaged trade impose additional human costs. Plant as visual stakes, not a speech.

summary: Tali chooses to expose her hidden transit network only after warning affected households, and is lost from communications while protecting incoming refugees. Jex's influence strategy carries intimate consequences.
settingText: INT. JEX'S OFFICE / EXT. AURIC HIDDEN APERTURES

dialogueInline.speaker: Tali
dialogueInline.text: The families are moving. Open the network before the next transport reaches the ambush.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jex
dialogueInline.text: Once I send the route authentication, anyone watching the traffic can trace these private access points.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: I'll protect the ships from the Auric end. I can't cover Tali's safehouse.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tali
dialogueInline.text: I know what we're risking. There are people on those transports too.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jex
dialogueInline.text: All right. I'm opening the links.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: First ships are through. They're turning toward the shelter docks.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jex
dialogueInline.text: Tali, hostile traffic is converging on your location. Leave now.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tali
dialogueInline.text: Get the families out. I'm closing the last access here.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Her connection is gone.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jex
dialogueInline.text: That's a lost signal. It doesn't tell us whether she got away.

panelPlan: Tali helps evacuate people from her refuge and sends Jex an explicit readiness signal.
Jex authorizes physical corridor anchors and authenticated safe-route beacons, exposing the routes through the pattern of departing traffic.
Civilian transports follow the newly usable corridors to Auric while Verge escorts move to cover their arrival.
Hostile sensors converge on Tali's access location; she is seen closing the haven's last access after the families depart.
Tali's link disappears from the communication display; Jex cannot tell whether the signal failed or the haven was hit.
directionInline: The route release should feel irreversible. As concealed apertures activate, Tali's node becomes visible and then disappears; Jex must keep transmitting even after he realizes the cost has become personal.

directionInline.text: Do not visually imply Tali's death. Her disappearance must remain uncertainty, not an explosion or magical deletion. Preserve coherent scale of vessels, anchors, corridors and travel times.

directionInline: Route geometry, anchors, phase and timing are physical science. Tali has agency; Jex can't bargain away her risk.

summary: Billie and Pike exploit the ring heat crisis to stage a physically coherent assault on Richard's clinic. Billie has abandoned the limits of the earlier no-death cargo raid.
settingText: EXT./INT. AURIC LUXURY RING — UNDER ATTACK

dialogueInline.speaker: Pike
dialogueInline.text: Auric moved its defense ships toward the arriving refugees. The ring's service side is exposed.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: Then put the boarding craft at the maintenance access. I'm taking Richard out of that clinic.

dialogueInline.speaker: Pike
dialogueInline.text: His records have already spread beyond Auric.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: Then I'll make him answer for them where everyone can hear.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: Get down! Away from the glass!

dialogueInline.speaker: Paul
dialogueInline.text: Those are Shard markings. They've come for Dad.

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: Move the patients first. We'll go with them.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: The clinic is past that pressure corridor. Bring the boarding craft alongside.

panelPlan: Billie and Pike's force approaches outside the Auric ring while civilian ships and escorts cross exposed approaches.
A compact Shard boarding craft separates from the assault formation and aligns with an actual maintenance access; Ashfang Marauder remains outside rather than physically crashing through the ring.
Pike directs suppressing fire toward defensive targets and evacuation escorts while Billie leaves the command space aboard the boarding craft.
Inside Auric, Tess and Paul move patients away from damaged glass as nearby systems shake from the strike.
The boarding craft locks onto a service port; Billie and a small team enter the pressurized maintenance passage leading toward Richard's clinic.
directionInline: Keep the attack attached to the evacuation geometry. Billie and Pike are not simply attacking Auric; they are forcing civilians to cross exposed space while hunting Richard inside the same structure.

directionInline.text: Supply the missing physical path from Billie's warship to the clinic used in P26. She boards via a smaller craft, not by driving a large named vessel through a station wall. Preserve named ship geometry and show civilian vulnerability without impossible collision scale.

directionInline: Billie remains recognizable and human, not a pirate caricature. Preserve boarding and vessel geometry and responsibility for the civilian threat.

summary: Six Shard captains voluntarily break with Billie's raid force and follow Abby into Verge-led civilian defense. They choose risk to their cultural standing; Abby cannot command them by rank.
settingText: INT. AURIC ESCORT CONTROL / ABBY'S SHUTTLE

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: Six captains chose to leave Billie's formation. They'll cover the refugee transports.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Yesterday you claimed more ships than that.

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: Six agreed. Others refused me. That's what I can offer.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: The shelter docks are full. We can't wait for Fleet to return.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Then your six fly under Verge coordination, inside this defense line only. Civilians first. No pursuit.

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: Understood. Where do you need the shields?

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Around the transports coming off Jex's routes. Leave the fight if getting civilians out requires it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: Send me their transponders. I'll put our ships between them and Pike.

panelPlan: Evacuation craft fill Naomi's displays.
Abby offers the six captains who voluntarily joined her civilian-protection plan.
Naomi rejects broad command access.
She assigns civilian shield duty.
Abby transmits Naomi's proposed shield positions to the independent captains who agreed to coordinate.
directionInline: Naomi accepts Abby's help only after narrowing its purpose to civilian protection. Abby's frustration should remain, but the tactical display must show her ships moving into the assigned shield positions rather than pursuing enemies.

directionInline.text: Emphasize the practical agreement and its limits: Abby's six ships protect transports, not attack freely or gain command of Auric. Keep Shard and Verge ship markings distinct.

directionInline: The Shards are a confederation. Each captain retains their own crew and ship; allegiance is negotiated, not an order from Abby.

summary: The Verge and six Shard captains defend civilian craft together while Fleet officer Deka independently confronts the command-versus-consequence decision made by Venn.
settingText: EXT. AURIC BAZAAR — RINGSPACE BATTLE

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Civilian Three, turn toward the gold strut. Your escort is coming across your bow.

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: My ships will take the fire. Keep the transports moving.

dialogueInline.speaker: Pilot
dialogueInline.text: There are families aboard. We can't outrun them.

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: You don't have to. Keep your course while we cover you.

dialogueInline.speaker: Deka
dialogueInline.text: Thunderbreak has a clear view of the evacuation route. Those transports are under attack.

dialogueInline.speaker: Officer
dialogueInline.text: Our orders are to remain outside Auric's boundary. Venn's suspension is still in force.

dialogueInline.speaker: Deka
dialogueInline.text: I know the order. Put the civilian ships on the main display.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Thunderbreak, if you can hear us, we need your help. They're hitting unarmed transports.

panelPlan: Escorts thread luminous ring architecture.
Abby's ships take fire for refugee craft.
Workers launch rescue skiffs by hand.
Thunderbreak holds beyond the boundary.
Deka watches a civilian ship tumble toward fire.
directionInline: The coalition should look improvised and unequal: Verge escorts, Abby's defectors, worker skiffs and Thunderbreak outside jurisdiction all solve different parts of the same emergency. No formation should suddenly look like a unified fleet.

directionInline.text: Establish that Deka is physically aboard and in acting authority, Venn is away at tribunal, and the ship is outside the defensive line. Naomi explicitly asks for help; no empty 'Commodore—' exchange.

directionInline: Deka remains a sincere trained Core officer, not a reckless mutineer. Shard/Verge/Fleet hull identities and shields must remain physically consistent.

summary: Dominion offers Venn reinstatement if she supports a controlled Fleet withdrawal and civilian witness custody. He believes this will contain conflict; Venn opposes coercing Auric's witness, and Deka independently takes Thunderbreak toward endangered civilians.
settingText: INT. ADMIRALTY TRIBUNAL / THUNDERBREAK BRIDGE

dialogueInline.speaker: Dominion
dialogueInline.text: I can restore your command of Thunderbreak if you back a withdrawal and bring Secundo under Fleet protection for testimony.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: Secundo is a civilian witness. Auric hasn't surrendered its authority over him.

dialogueInline.speaker: Keating
dialogueInline.text: We're trying to keep one emergency from becoming an inter-faction war.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: No. Auric can't be protected by handing him over.

dialogueInline.speaker: Dominion
dialogueInline.text: Then your suspension stands. You have no authority to command that ship.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: I understand. Lieutenant Deka, my suspension hasn't been lifted. I cannot order you into Auric.

dialogueInline.speaker: Deka
dialogueInline.text: We can see the transports being hit, Commodore.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: You and your officers will have to decide what responsibility you have to them.

dialogueInline.speaker: Deka
dialogueInline.text: Helm, cross the boundary. Put us between the refugees and the attackers.

panelPlan: Battle footage fills the tribunal.
Dominion presents restoration orders.
Venn leaves them untouched.
Her unauthorized channel reaches Thunderbreak.
Deka advances the ship across the boundary.
directionInline: Dominion's offer must be visibly attractive: command restored, legal authority returned, a route out of chaos. Venn refuses the bargain and then deliberately stops short of issuing an unlawful order, leaving Deka's crossing as the crew's choice.

directionInline.text: The command transfer is central: Venn DOES NOT order the ship across. Deka consciously assumes operational responsibility despite Admiralty restrictions. Show the tribunal and bridge as two distinct spaces connected by a call, with no magically restored rank or command.

directionInline: Dominion's goal of lasting Fleet corridor authority can benefit from fear of inadequate protection, but he neither needs to admit nor consciously seek suffering. He sincerely considers stability and command legitimate goals.
Venn remains Core-loyal and accepts authority; she refuses to command Deka illegally. Deka bears responsibility for her own choice.

summary: Billie and Tess confront each other at the clinic as close lifelong sisters-in-arms, not a rebellious subordinate versus commander. Their disagreement becomes painful because they really are family.
settingText: INT. LUXURY RING — CLINIC PRESSURE CORRIDOR

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: Move aside, Tess. I'm taking Secundo. He can tell everyone what his records really mean.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: He published the records. Taking him won't put them back in the box.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: You helped Abby turn my captains against me.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: I stayed here. You never once asked what I'd found in this clinic.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: She's your sister. I thought I was family too.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: You are. That's why I kept hoping you'd see what was happening here.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: I asked you to come home.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: And leave them here for you to collect?

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: Then are you going to let me pass?

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: Richard and the patients are staying. Turn around.

panelPlan: Show the service airlock behind Billie opening into the clinic pressure corridor; Shard boarders remain visible at the docked craft.
Tess steps between Billie and the patient area while Richard and Paul evacuate vulnerable patients beyond the door.
Billie demands Richard and advances, but Tess refuses to abandon the clinic or surrender the medical records.
Billie and Tess struggle at close range in the narrow passage, each attempting to control the route to the clinic rather than posing heroically.
Their fight damages the already stressed pressure window; Billie is wounded and the barrier begins to fail, leaving both women exposed.
directionInline: The fight must read as intimacy turned physical. Billie and Tess know each other's habits, but Tess is no longer using that familiarity to excuse her. Pressure damage around them keeps the fight dangerous to everyone nearby.

directionInline.text: Billie's arrival must follow the boarding route shown on P22. Keep Richard and Paul visible beyond Tess, retreating with patients. The conflict concerns a specific attempted seizure, not a sequence of abstract family epigrams.

directionInline: Tess is both Abby's sister and Billie's chosen family; disagreement does not erase familiarity. Keep focus on patients and shared history.

summary: Richard treats the wounded Billie despite her attempted abduction; Pike withdraws without her, Abby offers a way out, and Billie declines. Care crosses faction lines without absolving wrongdoing.
settingText: INT./EXT. CLINIC BREACH / AURIC RING

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: Leave it, doctor. You'd be safer if I bled out.

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: Maybe. But you're bleeding in front of me, and I can stop it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Paul
dialogueInline.text: She came to drag you out of the clinic.

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: I know. Help me hold the dressing while Tess seals that window.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: Pike's force is withdrawing. He isn't answering Billie's signal.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: He'll come for his ships.

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: His ships are leaving you behind. Take my hand. There's still time.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: You think carrying me out makes everything all right?

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: No. It means you live long enough to answer for what you did.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: I'm not going anywhere with you.

panelPlan: Richard and Paul apply a pressure dressing to Billie's wound while Tess works to stabilize the corridor's ruptured pressure window.
A view of the disengaging Shard assault reveals Pike's ships turning away from Billie's distress signal.
Abby arrives from a small escort shuttle newly docked at a safe service access; she enters the same corridor instead of appearing without an approach.
Abby offers to evacuate Billie but makes no promise of forgiveness or freedom from consequences.
Billie pulls away and reaches the boarding craft's independent emergency launch capsule while Richard and Tess protect the remaining patients; her eventual whereabouts are unresolved.
directionInline: Richard treats Billie while Paul objects, preserving the medical ethic that has defined him since Mercy of Dawn. Abby's offered hand is rescue without forgiveness; Billie's refusal keeps her outside reconciliation.

directionInline.text: Clearly distinguish stopping Billie's bleeding from absolving her. Abby must travel physically to the corridor from the escort defense, not teleport. Billie escapes using a plausible emergency launch connected to her already established boarding craft.

directionInline: Abby's appeal is made to a dear friend and fellow independent captain, not a subordinated officer.

summary: Auric survives with ongoing housing, warmth, ship-repair and medical shortages; Shard civilian defenders have helped, while Fleet tribunal formally removes Venn.
settingText: INT./EXT. AURIC BAZAAR — AFTERMATH

dialogueInline.speaker: Sera
dialogueInline.text: The damaged ring is holding pressure. We've got people sealing the smaller breaches.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: How many families can stay in the heated sections tonight?

dialogueInline.speaker: Sera
dialogueInline.text: Enough to keep moving people out of the exposed rooms. We'll need more space tomorrow.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: The transports got through because Abby's ships took the first hits.

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: Tess, can you leave the clinic now?

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: Not while we've still got patients coming in.

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: The Tal Corvus records have been copied beyond Auric. They can't quietly erase them now.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kerr
dialogueInline.text: The tribunal's finding is removal from command. The order is effective immediately.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: Then the Admiralty can put my reasons beside its decision.

panelPlan: Incompatible ships hold amid debris.
Locals and refugees carry wounded together.
Dain and Halev reopen shared shelter.
Abby watches Tess remain at the clinic.
Venn hears the guilty finding as testimony spreads behind her.
directionInline: Do not stage the aftermath as a victory tableau. Each faction has lost something: Venn command, Abby unity, Tess family certainty, Auric infrastructure. The meaningful success is that civilians and evidence survived.

directionInline.text: Do not present the coalition as a clean military victory or make the ring perfectly repaired. The tribunal finding is formally distinct from Venn's earlier temporary suspension. The survivors still lack enough heated space.

directionInline: Partial relief is real but not a cure. Maintain ring damage, crowding and dwindling heating capacity rather than resetting Auric to pristine luxury.

summary: Halev and Auric adopt voluntary civilian residency and defense with independently consenting Shard captains, without ceding permanent control to Fleet. Jex faces Tali's unknown fate and future responsibility for the raiding-and-protection cycle.
settingText: INT. AURIC CIVIC CHAMBER / JEX'S OFFICE

dialogueInline.speaker: Sera
dialogueInline.text: Shelter can't stop at tonight. People need permission to live here, not just wait for another departure.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: We'll offer residency to the Tal Corvus families who want it. Auric will have to fund the housing and repairs.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Our defense agreement can't give Fleet permanent authority over Auric. We just saw what their orders cost us.

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: And no Shard captain can claim a family because they once lived under our protection.

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: Witnesses who came here seeking safety stay under Auric's protection. No forced return.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: What do we do when another attack comes?

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Auric calls the escorts and the captains who agreed to defend civilians. We respond together, with Auric in charge of its own station.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jex
dialogueInline.text: Tali's safehouse is empty. The channel is still dead.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: Do you know if she got out?

dialogueInline.speaker: Jex
dialogueInline.text: No. And I won't call her dead because a signal went missing.

panelPlan: A mixed public chamber reconvenes.
Dain enters the shelter guarantee.
Halev strikes permanent Fleet authority.
The principals assent to mutual civilian defense.
Jex receives TALI STATUS UNKNOWN.
directionInline: The compact should emerge as a list of limits and obligations rather than a triumphant constitution. Jex's Tali alert should intrude at the end, making the new public order coexist with a private unresolved cost.

directionInline.text: This is the FIRST creation of the civilian-defense compact in Issue 3, not a pact already established before P01. Make terms specific, non-magical and voluntary. No premature certainty about Tali.

directionInline: Do not resolve the deeper cycle: Shard scarcity motivates raids, raids increase Verge demand for Fleet protection, Fleet patrols can deepen Shard exclusion. Stolen supplies feed Shard families as well as harming their original recipients; Jex may eventually reveal the full accounting.
Halev leads Auric and chairs the wider Verge council; the compact does not automatically bind all Verge communities or all independent Shard captains.

summary: Venn leaves under Fleet disciplinary orders while Naomi reports Auric's fragile self-governing compact. Venn remains a believer shaped by the BHA, proto-Fleet and Core service traditions, even as she confronts their unseen human costs.
settingText: INT. FLEET DETENTION TRANSIT / AURIC OBSERVATION GLASS

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Auric approved residency. Some of those families may still be sleeping in the freight hall next month.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: Halev told me he couldn't offer them permanent rooms.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: He can't. But they voted to stop treating the families as temporary cargo.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: And Fleet jurisdiction?

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: None permanently. Abby's captains can help, but Auric decides when.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: The Admiralty will have questions about the compact.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: I know. I was angry when you left. I was angrier when I started wondering if you were glad to go.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: Some mornings I was relieved to get one clear order. That didn't make your problems go away.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: You could have told me that.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: I should have. I'm being sent away without Thunderbreak, but I'll keep looking for a way back.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Then come back with something Auric can actually use.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: I'll try. I won't promise more than that.

panelPlan: Venn sits in a spare detention-transit compartment without insignia; Naomi stands near Auric observation glass.
Their permitted call begins with the still-precarious residency vote, not a triumphal report.
The subject turns from the agreement to Naomi's anger at Venn's absence and Venn's guilty relief at being sent away; hold faces rather than inserting more screens.
Venn can promise neither command nor immediate return. Their last lines acknowledge the unresolved distance.
End on their two separate views of incompatible ships guarding the same shelter lights.
directionInline: Keep Venn's detention visible throughout the call: no insignia, restricted compartment, permitted connection. Naomi's invitation is affectionate but not absolution; the final image of incompatible ships guarding the same shelter should carry the larger promise.

directionInline.text: No smug epigrams about unofficial things, no implied restoration of Venn's authority, and no instant resolution of their personal disagreement. The closing emotional beat is a concrete intention to try returning under changed circumstances.

directionInline: Venn must not become an anti-Fleet ideological hero. Both she and Dominion are sincere, yet both habitually count Verge/Fleet victims without equally registering Shard families receiving redirected supplies.
